claim_type_rationale: Universe = 18 curator-selected decisive WWI battles from the master article's broad-incomplete enumeration of hundreds of engagements (the master explicitly says 'this list is incomplete' covering battles, campaigns, operations, defensive positions, and sieges). The 18-row curator-balanced selection across 6 fronts is curator-judgment; the per-row attribute values (Year, Front, Strategic Outcome, Commanders) are sourced from per-battle Wikipedia articles. Multi-hop framing: each cell except Battle PK requires cross-source resolution (master defines the universe; per-battle articles supply the values). Same source-pattern + claim_type as the sibling `decisive_battles_of_world_war_ii` instance (which is also partially_supplemented with source_count=19).

collection_summary.approach: Pre-curation design pass (cycle-0 source exploration + audit-cycle-1 design review APPROVE-WITH-AMENDMENTS) produced a source-faithful instance. PIVOT context: the prior `worlds_longest_railway_tunnels_with_country_and_completion_decade` candidate was REJECTED as multi_hop by audit-cycle-1 (Country + Year same-row master attributes; Decade mechanical derivation = top_k/projection, not multi_hop). The WWI battles pivot inherits the WWII-approved multi_hop framing: per-battle source-join for commander + outcome cells. Audit-cycle-1 issued 7 required amendments + 10 per-question rulings + an 18-row universe suggestion — all incorporated. Staged design is locked.

universe_listing.note: Cycle-2 fix: Outcome corrected from 'Entente' to 'Contested / Mixed' per audit cycle-1 finding — article infobox Result = 'Indecisive'; Contested / Mixed matches the staged 3-value vocab without a strategic-Entente override claim.

Multi-year campaign 1915-1916; staged with start year 1915 per multi-year-start convention. Front classified under Middle Eastern Theatre per audit-cycle-1 amendment #5 (NOT a separate Gallipoli front). Cycle-2 fix: Central Powers Commander corrected from 'Otto Liman von Sanders' to 'Enver Pasha' per audit cycle-1 finding — article infobox first-listed Central Powers commander is Enver Pasha (Ottoman War Minister); Liman von Sanders was operational commander of Ottoman Fifth Army defending Gallipoli but not first-listed.

Cycle-2 fix: Entente Commander corrected from 'Radko Dimitriev' to 'Grand Duke Nicholas' (Russian commander-in-chief, first-listed in infobox); Central Powers Commander corrected from 'August von Mackensen' to 'Erich von Falkenhayn' (German Chief of Staff, first-listed) per audit cycle-1 finding. Mackensen was operational commander of 11th Army but not first-listed.

Strategically a British (Entente) victory — German High Seas Fleet retreated; tactically a German victory — German fleet inflicted more tonnage losses. Staged as Contested / Mixed per audit-cycle-1 amendment #4.

Multi-year context: Jul 1 - Nov 18 1916. Strategic outcome contested — Entente attackers gained limited ground but inflicted heavy German casualties; the 'big push' did not achieve breakthrough but is sometimes credited with weakening German army for 1918 collapse. Staged as Contested / Mixed per audit-cycle-1 amendment #4.

Feb-Dec 1916. French held Verdun against German offensive; recognized as Entente strategic victory. Pétain was operational commander early in the battle (Robert Nivelle assumed late-1916 command); Pétain is the article-lead foregrounded operational commander.
Cycle-2 fix: Central Powers Commander corrected from 'Alexander von Linsingen' to 'Conrad von Hötzendorf' (Austro-Hungarian Chief of Staff, first-listed in infobox) per audit cycle-1 finding.

Jul-Nov 1917. Also known as Third Battle of Ypres. BEF captured Passchendaele village but at catastrophic cost; strategic outcome is contested in historiography. Staged as Contested / Mixed per audit-cycle-1 amendment #4 illustration list.
Cycle-2 fix: Central Powers Commander corrected from 'Stefan Nerezov' to 'Georgi Todorov' (Bulgarian Second Army commander, first-listed in infobox) per audit cycle-1 finding.

Mar-Jul 1918. Final major German offensive on Western Front; tactical German gains but strategic failure as Allies recovered. Foch became Allied supreme commander during the offensive. Strategic Outcome = Entente (offensive failed to achieve war-winning breakthrough).
Aug-Nov 1918. Final Allied offensive ending the war. Decisive Entente victory leading to German armistice request.

collection_summary.commander_repetitions: Several commanders appear in multiple battle rows reflecting per-side operational command continuity across 1914-1918: Ferdinand Foch 3 times (German spring offensive, Second Marne, Hundred Days — Allied supreme commander); Erich Ludendorff 4 times (Passchendaele, German spring offensive, Second Marne, Hundred Days — German operational command); Douglas Haig 2 times (Somme, Passchendaele — BEF commander); Erich von Falkenhayn 3 times (First Ypres 1914, Gorlice–Tarnów 1915, Verdun 1916 — German Chief of Staff; cycle-2 fix added Gorlice–Tarnów occurrence per audit cycle-1 amendment). Otto Liman von Sanders 1 time (Megiddo 1918 only — cycle-2 fix removed Gallipoli per audit cycle-1 amendment, replaced with Enver Pasha).

decision_log.decision: Strategic Outcome column (3-value vocab) per audit-cycle-1 amendments #3 + #4
decision_log.rationale: Cycle-0 proposed 'Winning Side' with 2-value 'Entente' / 'Central Powers' mirroring WWII's 'Allied' / 'Axis'. Audit-cycle-1 amendment #3+#4: WWI has too many canonical-decisive battles with inconclusive/mixed-result outcomes (Somme 1916, Jutland 1916 strategic-Entente-vs-tactical-German, Passchendaele 1917, First Ypres 1914). 3-value vocab 'Entente / Central Powers / Contested / Mixed' more honestly captures the strategic-outcome semantics. Distribution (post-cycle-2 fixes): Entente 10, Central Powers 4, Contested / Mixed 4.

decision_log.decision: Front (theater) column 6-value vocab per audit-cycle-1 amendment #5
decision_log.rationale: Cycle-0 proposed 6-value vocab including 'Gallipoli' as separate front. Audit-cycle-1 amendment #5: do NOT make Gallipoli a front value — Gallipoli is classified under Middle Eastern Theatre per Wikipedia's geographic theater partition. Final 6-value vocab: Western Front (8 battles), Eastern Front (3), Italian Front (2), Middle Eastern Theatre (2 — Gallipoli + Megiddo), Balkan Front (1 — Dobro Pole), Naval (2 — Jutland + Falkland Islands).

decision_log.decision: Start-year convention for multi-year engagements per audit-cycle-1 amendment #6
decision_log.rationale: Multi-year battles staged with their start year: Gallipoli 1915 (multi-year 1915-1916), Verdun 1916 (Feb-Dec 1916), Somme 1916 (Jul-Nov 1916), Passchendaele 1917 (Jul-Nov), German spring offensive 1918 (Mar-Jul), Hundred Days 1918 (Aug-Nov). Mirrors WWII battles instance's multi-year handling (Moscow 1941-42 → 1941; Stalingrad 1942-43 → 1942; etc.). Multi-year battle date ranges documented in per-row universe_listing notes.

decision_log.rationale: Mirrors WWII battles instance's commander selection convention. First per-side operational commander from per-battle article infobox/lead. Curator overrides documented per row in universe_listing notes for cases like Verdun (Pétain early-1916 / Nivelle late-1916 → Pétain per article-lead operational-command convention).

open_questions.question: Per-row commander cell values are best-knowledge initial commits — should cycle-1 post-staging audit verify each against per-battle Wikipedia article infobox/lead?
open_questions.answer: Yes — per audit-cycle-1 amendment #7: 'first per-side operational commander from per-battle article infobox/lead; document overrides and alternatives per row'. Cycle-1 post-staging audit should verify each of the 36 commander cells (2 per battle × 18 battles) against the per-battle Wikipedia article. Likely audit-finding-candidates: Verdun (Pétain vs Nivelle late-1916), First Ypres (John French vs Ferdinand Foch debate), Gallipoli (Hamilton vs Birdwood for British operational command), Gorlice–Tarnów (Russian commander identification — Radko Dimitriev is one candidate, others possible).

open_questions.question: Should Passchendaele 1917 be staged as Entente (formal Allied victory at Passchendaele village capture) or Contested / Mixed (catastrophic-cost qualifies as mixed)?
open_questions.answer: Staged as Contested / Mixed per audit-cycle-1 amendment #4 illustration list (audit explicitly cited Passchendaele as a candidate for Contested / Mixed). Historiography varies; the staged value reflects the strategic-cost ambiguity. If cycle-1 post-staging audit prefers strict-victor framing, the cell would change to Entente.

open_questions.question: Are there other curator-balance candidates that could replace any of the 18 staged battles (e.g., Battle of the Frontiers 1914, Battle of Lemberg 1914, Battle of Tsingtao 1914, etc.)?
open_questions.answer: The 18-row universe was audit-suggested verbatim per cycle-1 amendment + suggested universe. Future-cycle audit could refine the universe (add/remove battles), but the current 18 is the audit's recommendation and the cycle-1 design-locked baseline.

open_questions.question: For multi-year battles, should Year staging include the end year as well (Year Range column)?
open_questions.answer: No — staged as start year only per audit-cycle-1 amendment #6 (mirrors WWII multi-year convention). Multi-year ranges documented in universe_listing per-row notes for transparency.
